pairs.locus: Albertanus, De amore et dilectione, lib. IV, cap. I (De iustitia), Seneca quote
pairs.question: Sequitur autem ratio naturam. Quid est ergo ratio?
pairs.derivation: Within the Seneca quotation the author poses a self-answered question. Setup 'Sequitur autem ratio naturam' is kept verbatim so 'ratio' has a referent; the question is the interrogative 'Quid est ergo ratio?' The answer is the immediately following two-word reply 'Nature imitatio.', stopping at its full stop before the text turns to a new definition ('Aliter eciam diffinitur...'). Dropped the surrounding framing 'de qua Seneca in epistolis dixit'.
